note: Uno calibration run: the same framework as Azul run1 (3x512 MLP, batched self-play). Trains on single hands, is RATED over 500-point matches. What we are after is the SHAPE of the Elo curve from zero, not the ceiling.
_note_game: Two specs over one engine (ludometer/games.py). A match to 500 is ~20 near-independent hands, so a match label is nearly noise for a move played in hand 3 - but a per-hand label is not a value function either: it resets at every hand boundary, and a search bootstrapping through one sees WINNING a hand as a fall from +1 to 0 and steers away from it (measured on a first attempt: value 0.75 one card from going out, 0.02 immediately after going out). So the training episode is one hand, where the label is the episode's own result, and the rating unit stays the full match, where 20 hands of deal luck cancel. The encoding carries no match score or hand number, so the same net is in-distribution for both.
_note_selfplay: batched (run5's engine) purely for throughput - each tree still searches sequentially, so a game is what the run1-era loop would have played. 4 drivers x 32 concurrent hands (measured: 77 matches/min at 128 concurrent, and a hand is ~1/26th of a match).
_note_search: 96 sims against run1's 160 is not a cut in search QUALITY: Uno offers 3.2 legal moves on average against Azul's 20-60, so 96 simulations look several plies deep where run1's 160 barely covered the root's children. Only ~40% of moves are searched at all - the rest are forced draws with one legal action.
_note_stall: A hand always terminates and there is only ever one of them per episode, so the anti-stall sampling is switched off. max_game_moves is the truncation backstop against a ~42-move hand.
_note_budget: 120,000 hands is ~17 searched decisions each, i.e. ~2.0M decisions against run1's 24,576 games x 52 = 1.28M. Sized on decisions rather than games because a hand and an Azul game are not the same amount of practice - see the note in NOTES_FOR_REMI.md on which x axis the cross-game comparison should use.
_note_eval: Uno's own ladder (uno:random pinned at 0), rated over full matches to 500 at 64 sims. A match is itself a low-variance measurement - 20 hands of deal luck largely cancel - so 32 games buy a tight error bar despite the game's randomness.
